destinations.name: Cox's Bazar
destinations.blurb: A seaside town on the Bay of Bengal, known for its very long sandy beach.

destinations.name: Sundarbans
destinations.blurb: A vast mangrove forest shared with India and home to the Royal Bengal tiger; a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

destinations.name: Saint Martin's Island
destinations.blurb: A small coral island in the Bay of Bengal, near Teknaf.

destinations.name: Sajek Valley
destinations.blurb: A hill valley in the Chittagong Hill Tracts (Rangamati district), known for clouds and long views.

destinations.name: Kaptai Lake
destinations.blurb: A large artificial lake in Rangamati, created by a dam on the Karnaphuli river.

destinations.name: Ratargul Swamp Forest
destinations.blurb: A freshwater swamp forest near Gowainghat, best explored by boat in the rainy season.

destinations.name: Jaflong
destinations.blurb: A hill-and-river area on the Meghalaya border in Sylhet.

destinations.name: Sreemangal
destinations.blurb: Known as the tea capital of Bangladesh, surrounded by tea estates.

destinations.name: Tanguar Haor
destinations.blurb: A large freshwater wetland in Sunamganj, important for migratory birds.

destinations.name: Kuakata
destinations.blurb: A beach in Patuakhali where you can watch both sunrise and sunset over the sea.

destinations.name: Somapura Mahavihara (Paharpur)
destinations.blurb: Ruins of a major Buddhist monastery in Naogaon; a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

destinations.name: Mahasthangarh
destinations.blurb: Ruins of an ancient city near Bogura, among the earliest urban sites in Bangladesh.

destinations.name: Puthia Temple Complex
destinations.blurb: A cluster of historic Hindu temples in Rajshahi district.

destinations.name: Mosque City of Bagerhat
destinations.blurb: A historic mosque city including the Sixty Dome Mosque; a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

destinations.name: Lalbagh Fort
destinations.blurb: A 17th-century Mughal fort complex in old Dhaka.

destinations.name: Ahsan Manzil
destinations.blurb: The pink palace on the Buriganga river, once the residence of the Dhaka Nawab family.

destinations.name: Sonargaon
destinations.blurb: A historic town near Dhaka that was an important centre in medieval Bengal.

history.title: Early kingdoms and the Pala era
history.text: The region that is now Bangladesh was home to early Bengal kingdoms such as Pundravardhana and Vanga. In the 8th century the Pala dynasty ruled; the great monastery of Somapura Mahavihara at Paharpur was built under Dharmapala.

history.title: The Bengal Sultanate
history.text: Between the 14th and 16th centuries Bengal was ruled by independent sultans, a period of trade, architecture and the growth of Bengali literature.

history.title: Dhaka becomes a Mughal capital
history.text: In 1610 Dhaka became the provincial capital of Mughal Bengal under Islam Khan I, and grew into a major trading city.

history.title: Battle of Plassey
history.text: In 1757 the East India Company defeated the Nawab of Bengal at Plassey, beginning British dominance in Bengal that lasted until 1947.

history.title: Partition of Bengal
history.text: Lord Curzon partitioned Bengal in 1905, creating a province with Dhaka as its capital. It was annulled in 1911 after widespread protest.

history.title: Partition of India
history.text: In 1947 the eastern part of Bengal became East Bengal, later East Pakistan, within the new state of Pakistan.

history.title: The Language Movement
history.text: On 21 February 1952 students and citizens in Dhaka protested for Bangla to be a state language and were fired upon. The day is remembered as Ekushey February; UNESCO proclaimed 21 February International Mother Language Day in 1999.

history.title: The Liberation War
history.text: Independence was declared on 26 March 1971 and the war ended with victory on 16 December 1971, now celebrated as Victory Day.

history.title: The Constitution
history.text: The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution of Bangladesh on 4 November 1972; it came into effect on 16 December 1972.

culture.title: Pohela Boishakh
culture.text: The Bengali New Year, celebrated in Bangladesh on 14 April with fairs, processions and traditional food.

culture.title: Rabindranath Tagore and Kazi Nazrul Islam
culture.text: Tagore, the 1913 Nobel laureate in Literature, wrote the words of 'Amar Shonar Bangla', Bangladesh's national anthem. Kazi Nazrul Islam is the national poet of Bangladesh.

culture.title: Baul songs
culture.text: A mystical folk song tradition of Bengal that UNESCO recognises as intangible cultural heritage; Lalon Fakir is its best-known figure.

culture.title: Jamdani weaving
culture.text: A fine, hand-woven fabric from the Dhaka region, recognised by UNESCO as intangible cultural heritage.

culture.title: Mangal Shobhajatra
culture.text: A colourful procession held on Pohela Boishakh in Dhaka, recognised by UNESCO as intangible cultural heritage.

culture.title: Rickshaw art
culture.text: The painted decorations of Dhaka's cycle rickshaws, recognised by UNESCO as intangible cultural heritage in 2023.

culture.title: Nakshi kantha
culture.text: Embroidered quilts traditionally made from layers of old cloth, with stitched patterns that tell stories.
